hook: In mice, cerebellar outputs to the red nucleus support reach correction and learning; broader ones do not.
summary: In reaching mice, small corrective submovements appeared spontaneously or after neural perturbations. Closed-loop perturbation of red nucleus-projecting neurons was compensated and shifted future submovement timing, while perturbing the interposed nucleus broadly was neither compensated nor learned. Findings are in mice performing one reach task.
title: Dissociable cerebellar pathways for reach correction and learning.
